title: 014 - Super Mario Bros.
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Super Mario Bros.
items.description: The episode's game: Nintendo's 1985 side-scrolling platformer by Miyamoto and Tezuka, a launch title for the NES.

links.label: Super Mario Bros. - The Mushroom Kingdom
Super Mario Bros. - Super Mario Wiki

items.name: Famicom and NES
items.description: Nintendo's Japanese and North American versions of the console, which differ in hardware and in the Famicom's disk add-on.

items.name: Famicom Disk System
items.description: The Japan-only disk drive add-on for the Famicom, which the NES never got.

items.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
items.description: Nintendo designer credited as co-creator of Super Mario Bros.

items.name: Takashi Tezuka
items.description: Co-designer of Super Mario Bros., credited with much of what makes the game work.

items.name: Iwata Asks: Tezuka interview
items.description: Interview in which Takashi Tezuka describes the original concept for Super Mario Bros.

links.label: Iwata Asks: New Super Mario Bros. Wii, Vol. 2

items.name: Mario Bros.
items.description: The 1983 game whose steady sales led to Mario being put into Super Mario Bros.

items.name: Donkey Kong
items.description: The 1981 arcade game in which Mario first appeared, as Jumpman.

items.name: Donkey Kong Jr.
items.description: Arcade sequel in which the character gets the name Mario.

items.name: Wrecking Crew
items.description: Earlier Mario game from the same period as Mario Bros. and Donkey Kong.

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.description: The NES sequel, which includes Mario Bros.-style levels and often overshadowed the first game for kids who grew up with it.

items.name: Super Mario Maker
items.description: Level-building game where Buzzy Beetle helmets appear, and where early control ideas for Super Mario Bros. were discussed.

items.name: Super Mario Galaxy
items.description: 3D Mario game with a spin move, mentioned as a later take on attacking.

items.name: Ice Climber
items.description: Launch title with a poor jump compared to Mario's.

items.name: Kung Fu
items.description: Launch title whose jump and movement were compared unfavorably with Mario's.

items.name: Kirby's Dream Land
items.description: Game Boy game that was one host's first game.

items.name: Super Mario 64
items.description: The first 3D Mario game, played by one host as a small child before the NES original.

items.name: Super Mario All-Stars
items.description: SNES collection with graphically improved versions of the NES Mario games, where several hosts first played the original.

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: The show's running list of NES games still worth playing today; Super Mario Bros. was the first vote.

items.name: Lakitu
items.description: Cloud-riding enemy that throws Spinies, later the camera operator in Super Mario 64.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of Mario franchise enemies

items.name: Hammer Bros.
items.description: Hammer-throwing enemies considered among the toughest in the game.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of Mario franchise enemies

items.name: Bowser
items.description: The Koopa king and final boss, called the great demon king Koopa in Japan.

items.name: Koopa Troopa
items.description: Walking turtle enemy; green ones keep walking, red ones turn at ledges.

items.name: How to Win at Super Mario Bros.
items.description: Strategy book that gave away the game's secrets, later given to Nintendo Fun Club members.

links.label: How to Win at Super Mario Bros. - Super Mario Wiki

items.name: The Legend of Zelda
items.description: Nintendo's next big NES release, noted for vague clues, coming later in the series.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda (video game)

items.name: Princess Peach
items.description: The mushroom princess, called Princess Toadstool in the North American release.

items.name: Vs. System
items.description: Nintendo's arcade hardware line that many NES launch games first appeared on.

items.name: Vs. Super Mario Bros.
items.description: Arcade version with new levels, now playable on Nintendo Switch.

links.label: Vs. Super Mario Bros. - Killer List of Videogames

items.name: Super Mario Bros. Deluxe
items.description: Game Boy Color version with an overworld map, red coin challenges and a two-player mode.

items.name: Super Mario World
items.description: SNES launch game, part of the same lineage of Mario design.

items.name: Dark Souls
items.description: Used as a modern shorthand for hard games, compared to the NES term Nintendo hard.
